# Preface {.unnumbered}

> **Under construction.** Chapters are being written in course order; Act I (chapters 1–3) first.

This book teaches one habit: **before you analyze data, write down — as runnable code — the
process you think produced it.** Every chapter starts from a biological question, builds the
process that generates the data, plays with it, and only then compresses what you built into
notation. The formula is always the *last* form of an idea you have already run.

Every chapter ends with ungraded practice problems, **with worked solutions.** There is nothing
here you are graded on, by design: the course's problem sets are released separately, and this
book is fully open — to you, and to your AI tutor — precisely because it contains no answers to
anything that counts.

How to read it: run the code. Every chunk is seeded, so you will see exactly the figures printed
here — and then you should change the settings and see something the book has never seen.
